correctness.rationale: For commuting nondecreasing finite-chain retractions e,f the common product h=ef is an idempotent and its fibers are invariant rooted intervals. The side-exclusion lemma holds in both directions: two extra fixed points of different maps on the same side contradict commutativity; conversely one map constant at the root on each side makes both composites constant there. An anchored side of length a has H_a retractions, H(t)=(1-t)/(1-3t+t^2), so an ordered two-map side has 2H_a-1 choices. Each h-fiber has B(t)=tL(t)^2, L(t)=2H(t)-1/(1-t), yielding exactly the bivariate uB/(1-uB) and c_{n,k}=[t^{n-k}]L(t)^{2k}. Dominant-root analysis, positive aperiodic B coefficients and an ordinary pole justify the total-count and linear mean common-rank asymptotics. Exact B(1/6)=5766/9025<1 establishes exponential decay of commuting probability against F_{2n}^2. Independently enumerated ALL monotone idempotents and commuting ordered pairs through n=7 with every rank coefficient matching the renewal formula; finite checks do not prove the all-n claim.
